newsitem.title: JAPAN: Profit-taking weighs on U.S. Treasuries in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking weighs on U.S. Treasuries in Tokyo.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries fell slightly by Tokyo midday on Wednesday on light profit-taking after overnight rallies, traders said.

Follow-through buying was limited amid a lack of factors, with the dollar stuck near previous New York levels this morning. The technical climate turned brighter in the futures market after the overnight rise, but T-bond futures eased.

Treasuries rebounded on strong short-covering in New York on Tuesday, particularly pushing up the longer end of the market, after a relatively soothing speech by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.
The 6-1/2 percent 30-year bond stood at 96-9/32, yielding 6.79 percent, against 96-11/32 in New York on Tuesday.
March T-bond futures fell slightly to 111-14/32 from the previous close of 111-16/32.
"Further technical buying could keep prices well-supported," a trust bank trader said. "Technically, the market looks pretty good after yesterday's recovery."

Traders are looking forward to the release of employment cost index (ECI) for the fourth quarter, due for release next week, to see whether they are sure about the trend of the market in the longer term.
